nodes.label: Nature-based solutions

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Sustainable water resource management|Nature-based solutions_qna_000
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What does "NCP" stand for in the context of this paragraph?
nodes.answer: NCP stands for nature's contribution to people.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Sustainable water resource management|Nature-based solutions_qna_001
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What methodology was developed and applied in this study to prioritize Nature-based Solutions and Bioeconomy Solutions?
nodes.answer: A participatory, cross-sectoral multi-criteria assessment (MCA) decision-support tool was developed and applied.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Sustainable water resource management|Nature-based solutions_qna_002
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What solutions are suggested to address the effects of climate change in the Mediterranean region?
nodes.answer: The suggested solutions include the implementation of Nature-based Solutions (NBS) and Bioeconomy Solutions (BES) that focus on utilizing local natural resources and biowaste.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Sustainable water resource management|Nature-based solutions_qna_003
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What do Nature-based Solutions (NBS) and Bioeconomy Solutions (BES) emphasize?
nodes.answer: Nature-based Solutions (NBS) and Bioeconomy Solutions (BES) emphasize the importance of local natural resources and biowaste as part of the solutions to combat climate change.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Sustainable water resource management|Nature-based solutions_qna_004
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What do NBS approaches prioritize in their application?
nodes.answer: NBS approaches prioritize the conservation and restoration of natural systems as well as the creation of novel ecosystems to address societal and environmental challenges.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Sustainable water resource management|Nature-based solutions_qna_005
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: In what way can NBS and BES be applied together?
nodes.answer: NBS and BES can be applied separately or combined to effectively approach the Water-Food-Energy-Ecosystems (WEFE) nexus perspective in human activities.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Sustainable water resource management|Nature-based solutions_qna_006
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: In what contexts has MCA been widely applied?
nodes.answer: MCA has been widely applied in nature-based solutions (NBS) and built environment solutions (BES) in engineering, natural resources management, and climate adaptation and resilience.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Sustainable water resource management|Nature-based solutions_qna_007
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How does the presented methodology enable the evaluation and selection of NBS/BES solutions?
nodes.answer: The methodology utilizes a participatory MCA approach to evaluate, compare, select, and prioritize NBS/BES solutions that integrate the elements of the WEFE nexus.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Sustainable water resource management|Nature-based solutions_qna_008
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the significance of the case studies presented in the work?
nodes.answer: The case studies on Tinos Island in Greece demonstrate the customization and application of the NBS/BES tool in a real-world context.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Sustainable water resource management|Nature-based solutions_qna_009
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Why is the NBS/BES tool considered innovative in the context of Greece?
nodes.answer: To the best of the authors' knowledge, similar methodologies have not been developed or applied previously in Greece, making it a novel approach in that context.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Sustainable water resource management|Nature-based solutions_qna_010
nodes.question: Who are some of the authors of the report "A Nature-Positive World: the Global Goal for Nature"?
nodes.answer: Some of the authors include H. Locke, J. Rockström, P. Bakker, M. Bapna, M. Gough, and J. Lambertini.
